youtube.title: SHANE JONES
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with NZ First Deputy Leader Shane Jones about vote-splitting under MMP, criticising National’s opposition to the strategy and arguing that the centre-right should focus on winning voters through policy rather than attacking political personalities. Jones outlines NZ First’s priorities for economic growth, energy affordability, investment, law and order, immigration and national security. Discover more from Shane Jones or find him on Facebook and X For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday and find out everything about the overhang, wasted vote and tactical voting at Vote Smart

youtube.title: IVOR CUMMINS
youtube.summary: Ivor Cummins joins Paul Brennan from Dublin to discuss the prospect of conscription in Britain, public resistance to military service, and his view that escalating warnings about Russia are intended to influence public opinion. They also examine political elites, media narratives, free speech, protest movements and the erosion of critical thinking. Check out his YouTube talk with Eddie Hobbs | “Critical Thinking Can Save Us All”

youtube.title: EDWARD SCHULLER
youtube.summary: Michael Arbon speaks with Edward Schuller, National Secretary of the Teachers Professional Association of Australia, about Protect Our Kids, a campaign challenging sex education programmes delivered in Australian schools. Edward calls for greater parental oversight, funding cuts for organisations providing material he considers inappropriate, and major education reforms, including local school autonomy. Sign the petition to End Pornography in Classrooms or download the Free Action Kit Discover more from Edward on YouTube and X Find more from Michael on Facebook and X

youtube.title: LIAM HEHIR
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with political commentator Liam Hehir about the strategy of engineering an overhang under MMP by splitting electorate and party votes to boost the centre-right’s representation. Liam warns that the strategy could provoke retaliation from the left, undermine proportional representation and ultimately benefit Labour in future elections.
